summary: Joining several tables is just one join after another, each adding a table.
points: Each new JOIN needs its own ON linking it to a table already in the query.
Follow the keys like a path: customers to orders to order_items to products.
Build it one join at a time and check the rows at each step.
If any step must keep unmatched rows, later joins usually must be LEFT JOINs too.

example.sql:
SELECT c.name, p.name AS product, i.quantity
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id
JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id;
example.explanation: The query walks from customer to product through two linking tables.
